newsitem.title: USA: A.M. Best downgrades Pacificare's California unit.
newsitem.headline: A.M. Best downgrades Pacificare's California unit.

text.p: Insurance rating agency A.M. Best Co said Monday it lowered the rating of PacifiCare of California Inc from "A+" (Superior) to "A" (Excellent).

A.M. Best said the downgrade reflects the competitive nature of the California market, which accounts for about two-thirds of the membership of PacifiCare's parent organization -- PacifiCare Health Systems -- and an even more significant portion of the overall earnings.

It also said it reflects difficulties associated with the integration of FHP International Corp, high financial leverage resulting from PacifiCare's acquisition of FHP, and increasing competitive pressures on margins for the organization's Medicare-risk business.
A.M. Best said Pacificare must modify its provider contracting and network management to establish one consistent corporate philosophy.
It also said it must complete the prior FHP conversion of existing computer system technology onto one system, and convert that system into PacifiCare's operating system.

A.M. Best said the company's financial leverage currently is above average as a result of the FHP acquisition. It said the debt load, along with the amortization of the goodwill associated with the acquisition, will be another obstacle for future earnings.
